Thanks — digging in. Initial strawman/high level notes below (we should refine with infra team before sending to customer):

1) Baselines & assumptions:
- Model family: mid-sized open-chat model (approx resource footprint we typically benchmark).
- Serving efficiency: assume 60-70% utilization after batching and caching optimizations for chat-style workloads.
- Token mix: 60% prompt / 40% completion for their flows (useful for endpoint selection).

2) Unit economics (hosted) — rough before discounts (USD per 1M tokens):
- US region baseline: ~$850 per 1M tokens (hosted, multi-tenant)
- EU region baseline: +20% uplift vs US due to higher infra/egress/operational costs => ~$1,020 per 1M tokens

3) Dedicated EU-only pool (committed capacity):
- With a 12-month minimum commit and predictable utilization, we could target ~15% discount vs EU hosted baseline => ~ $867 per 1M tokens effective for committed EU pool (includes KMS/HSM and audit retention).
- Break-even guidance: for their 3B tokens/mo, a dedicated EU pool starts to look attractive if >50% of traffic must stay in EU and they sign a 6-12 month commit.

4) Blended pricing example (hosted multi-region routing):
- If 60% of tokens routed to US and 40% to EU (per their user base), blended = 0.6*$850 + 0.4*$1,020 = ~$916 per 1M tokens — within their $1k–$1.2k target.

5) Other notes to highlight in customer-facing doc: 
- We should clearly call out what ‘EU residency’ covers (storage, logs, model cache residency, telemetry) and any limitations (cross-region fallbacks increase cost and latency).
- Call out optional add-ons that increase cost: long-term audit log retention, HSM-backed keys, enhanced network segmentation.

Next steps (internal): I’ll draft a short 1-page comparison (hosted blended vs dedicated EU) with the numbers above and a recommended ask for procurement (target commitment ranges to hit their blended target). Marissa — want me to send the draft to you before it goes to the customer?
